title: Primus Decision History record
description: One record per answered request, meant to be appended to a log: which model answered, what it was asked, what it answered and, once known, what the right answer was. Records are self-contained and ordered by `recorded_at`; a history is a sequence of them in any store (a JSON-lines file, a table, a queue). Readers must ignore `extensions` and must not require any property that is not listed as required here.

record_id.description: unique within the history; the producer chooses the scheme (UUID, ULID, content hash)

calibrated.description: true when the temperature profile was applied to the recorded probabilities

latency_ms.description: wall-clock time of the answer, when measured

outcomes.description: what turned out to be right, one entry per decision as it becomes known; absent until then

extensions.description: producer-specific data; never needed to read the record

weights_sha256.description: sha256 of model/ensemble.json for the ensemble (it names the member weights; every file's hash is in SHA256SUMS), or of model.safetensors when a single member answered

state.description: the state as sent (object or string), when keeping it is acceptable

state_sha256.description: sha256 of the state's canonical JSON text (UTF-8, keys sorted, separators ',' and ':'); use it instead of, or next to, `state`

option_keys.description: noul: ["false", "true"]; choice: the criteria keys in order; score: ["0", …, "n-1"]

probabilities.description: aligned with option_keys; sums to 1 within floating-point rounding

chosen.description: the option key with the largest probability; for noul, "true" iff its probability is at least 0.5

expected_score.description: score only: Σ level × probability; null for noul and choice

gold_label.description: the option key that turned out to be right

gold_probabilities.description: a soft target aligned with option_keys, when the source gives one
